content.value_statement: Medical device teams need clear regulatory strategy before they commit time and budget. This skill helps plan submissions, compliance work, timelines, and stakeholder communication.
actual_capabilities: Guides FDA, EU MDR, ISO, and global regulatory pathway planning from included reference material.
Structures submission preparation work across pre-submission, documentation, review, and post-market phases.
Helps identify regulatory risks, mitigation steps, milestones, and stakeholder responsibilities.
Provides KPI ideas for submission timelines, approval rates, inspection readiness, and team coordination.
Includes a Python tracker for local regulatory submission status reporting.
limitations: Does not replace legal counsel, notified body guidance, or direct regulator feedback.
Includes limited reference files and may mention resources that are not packaged.
Regulatory requirements change often and must be verified against current official sources.
The tracker stores local JSON data and is not a validated quality management system.

use_cases.title: Choose a submission pathway
use_cases.description: Compare FDA, EU MDR, and global options for a new medical device product plan.

use_cases.title: Prepare executive timelines
use_cases.description: Turn regulatory phases, review periods, and dependencies into a leadership-ready milestone plan.

use_cases.title: Coordinate cross-functional readiness
use_cases.description: Define quality, clinical, engineering, and operations inputs needed for a submission package.

prompt_templates.title: Start a pathway assessment
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me assess the likely regulatory pathway for this medical device. Product: [describe product]. Market: [target market]. Risk profile: [known risks].

prompt_templates.title: Build a submission checklist
prompt_templates.scenario: Create a practical work plan for a known pathway.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a submission preparation checklist for a [510(k), PMA, De Novo, or EU MDR] pathway. Include documents, owners, dependencies, and review checkpoints.

prompt_templates.title: Review regulatory risks
prompt_templates.scenario: Assess timeline, evidence, and compliance concerns.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this regulatory plan for risks and gaps. Plan: [paste plan]. Focus on evidence, documentation, authority interactions, and post-market obligations.

prompt_templates.title: Design a global strategy
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced planning across regions and teams.
prompt_templates.prompt: Develop a global regulatory strategy for this MedTech product across [regions]. Include pathway sequencing, submission dependencies, team responsibilities, and escalation points.

output_examples.input: Plan a 510(k) readiness review for a Class II monitoring device.
output: A pathway summary with predicate device analysis needs.
A documentation checklist covering performance testing, labeling, software, and quality records.
A readiness timeline with owner assignments and FDA interaction checkpoints.

output_examples.input: Find gaps in our EU MDR submission plan.
output: A gap list for clinical evidence, technical documentation, QMS readiness, UDI planning, and notified body engagement.
Suggested mitigation actions ranked by submission impact.
Questions to resolve before the next regulatory steering meeting.

output_examples.input: Create KPIs for regulatory leadership reporting.
output: Submission timeline adherence, first-pass acceptance, authority response cycle time, and inspection readiness metrics.
Suggested reporting cadence for weekly teams, monthly committees, and quarterly training reviews.

best_practices: Provide product classification, intended use, target market, and known evidence before asking for a strategy.
Validate all generated guidance against current official regulator sources before making decisions.
Use the output as a planning draft for review by qualified regulatory and legal professionals.
anti_patterns: Do not treat generated guidance as final legal or regulatory advice.
Do not submit documents without confirming current FDA, EU MDR, and local authority requirements.
Do not use the local tracker as a validated system of record for regulated quality processes.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps plan regulatory pathways, submission tasks, timelines, risks, and cross-functional coordination for HealthTech and MedTech products.

faq.question: Can it decide the correct FDA pathway?
faq.answer: It can help compare likely pathways, but final pathway decisions should be verified with current FDA guidance and qualified experts.

faq.question: Does it support EU MDR planning?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes EU MDR submission planning concepts such as classification, technical documentation, QMS, clinical evidence, UDI, and notified body review.

faq.question: Can it manage live submission data?
faq.answer: It includes a simple local Python tracker for JSON-based submission status reporting. It is not an enterprise regulatory information system.

faq.question: Is this suitable for startups?
faq.answer: Yes. It can help early teams structure market access planning, evidence needs, milestone reviews, and resource discussions.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
